edbDesc: A gas ionization process where an initially very small amount of free electrons, accelerated by a sufficiently strong electric field, give rise to electrical conduction through a gas by avalanche multiplication: when the number of free charges drops or the electric field weakens, the phenomena ceases.
title: Townsend discharge
description: In a gas under a strong voltage, one stray electron knocks loose others, which knock loose more, until a whole avalanche of charge rushes across. Townsend worked out this chain reaction around 1897, and it lets a Geiger counter turn the passage of one particle into a loud click.
effect: one free electron in a gas multiplies into an avalanche of charge
usedIn: Proportional counters and wire chambers in particle detectors
strength: A single electron can multiply into a million or more within a millimetre of travel, in less than a microsecond.
pickWhy: Specific effect that amplifies tiny signals; the deck's geiger-counter is a device built on it by a different person, so kept separate.
